text:
maya: quick summary from the 13B quant bakeoff (FP8/AWQ vs GPTQ vs INT8). dropping the deck + packaging recs for Redwood Optimize profiles.

devin: awesome, high level numbers?

maya: short table: AWQ-FP8 -> mean eval delta -0.8% (relative accuracy), latency 0.9x baseline for generation at 2048 tokens, memory down ~45%. GPTQ-INT4-ish -> delta -1.4%, latency 1.05x, mem -35%. INTACT INT8 (baseline optimized) -> delta -2.6%, latency 0.95x, mem -30%.

samir: interesting that AWQ-FP8 is both smaller and faster on our kernel set. were these runs with prefix caching on?

maya: yes caches enabled. workloads: mix of instruction-following, code-completion, and pairwise QA prompts. we tracked nll, exact-match style metrics and a small human-eval sample.

ingrid: how consistent are deltas across tasks? any big regressions on code?

maya: code tasks saw slightly higher regressions for AWQ-FP8 (~-1.6%) vs GPTQ (~-2.2%). FP8 helps on natural language but numeric stability + op coverage causes code diffs.

devin: from Optimize perspective we need: profile metadata (backend, bitwidth, per-op exclusions), a recommended rollout strategy and automatic fallback rules. can you paste the manifest sketch?

maya: pasted a minimal example below for the profile we think should be published to the registry:

```
qprofile_version: "1"
profile_name: "optimize-awq-fp8-13b-v0"
model_family: "llama-13b"
quant_backend: "awq"
bitwidth: "fp8"
ops_blacklist: ["flash_attn_backward_v2"]
expected_delta_percent: "-0.8"
recommended_rollout: "canary_5pct->gradual_50pct->full"
fallback_profile: "optimize-gptq-int8-13b-v0"
runtime_hints: ["enable_prefix_cache=true","batching_window_ms=8"]
```

samir: ops_blacklist is good. add a field `safety_checks` with a small evalset id to gate canary->50pct automatic promotion. also include `quant_tool_version` and `params_hash` so we can trace packaging to a specific bakeoff build.

maya: ack. suggested naming convention: `optimize-<backend>-<bitwidth>-<model>-v<semver>` to keep things consistent. e.g. `optimize-awq-fp8-13b-v0`. avoids ambiguous 'qpack' prefixes.

devin: naming is fine but recommend we also expose short canonical alias for runtime mapping (e.g. `opt:awq/fp8/13b/v0`) so routing policies are compact.

ingrid: from rollout/ops side we need an automatic fallback policy that will route to the fallback_profile if 5xx rate or token-error-rate crosses threshold for 120s. can we encode thresholds in the profile?

maya: yes add fields: `failure_threshold_5xx_pct=0.5`, `token_error_rate_threshold=0.2` (both percent), `evaluation_gate_evalset="qexp-2026-13b-core"`.

ci-bot: build queued: qprofile-optimize-awq-fp8-13b-v0 (job id 8421). logs: https://ci.internal/reports/8421

devin: packaging recs for Redwood Optimize UI: show delta, task-breakdown (nl/code/math), mem savings, latency multiplier, safe-list ops and blacklist ops, certifying bakeoff link. include an inline small chart: accuracy vs latency tradeoff.

samir: runtime note: AWQ-FP8 requires an adjusted kernel for rotary embeddings when seq_len>2048. add runtime_hint: `rotary_kernel_mode=stable_v2` to prevent NaNs.

maya: final ask: add `compat_matrix` field with runtime versions that pass (e.g. `runtime>=2.3` , `kernel-awq>=1.4`). we'll include consumer notes: "do not use for heavy code generation in current release; prefer GPTQ-int8 for code workloads until kernel updates".

devin: sounds actionable. i'll create the registry PR with the manifest and add the canary job to Redwood Optimize.

ingrid: once PR merged, ops will wire the circuit breaker and automatic fallback. thanks. :thumbsup:

maya: i'll upload the bakeoff artifacts and the evalset to S3 + attach the handbook snippet for rollout checks. will ping when CI finishes.

ci-bot: job 8421 completed: tests passed (smoke, integration, perf). artifact: s3://redwood-qprofiles/optimize-awq-fp8-13b-v0.tar.gz

devin: merging registry PR now. follow-up: add a short public blurb in Optimize UI that explains "expected delta" meaning and the evaluation matrix.

samir: small TODO: add a runtime flag to prefer `fallback_profile` automatically when median latency > 1.8x baseline for 60s. put that in a follow-up issue.
